title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Revit and AutoCAD Finish Schedules
summary: Use Gemini 4 Hydrogen to trace a flooring change across a bulletin, plan, and finish schedule, then carry the approved edit into Revit or AutoCAD.
body_markdown:
The finish bulletin changes the flooring in Room 214 from carpet tile to terrazzo. The finish schedule calls the room “West Meeting.” The plan calls it “Conference B.” A search for either name alone misses part of the change, while a global replacement of the carpet code would also change three offices where the carpet is staying.


This is the kind of everyday coordination job we’d give Gemini 4 Hydrogen. Google launched Hydrogen on November 12 as the fast member of the Gemini 4 family. It can work with PDFs and spreadsheets, and Google offers it through the Gemini API and Gemini app. In the free app, Google selects Hydrogen automatically for eligible requests.[Google’s Hydrogen launch and access details](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-hydrogen/)


## Gemini 4 Hydrogen for finish schedules and drawing revisions


Start with the bulletin, the current finish schedule, and the plan for the affected level. In this example, the room number gives Hydrogen a way to connect the records even when their names differ. If the project reuses numbers across buildings or phases, include those identifiers too.


> Compare the bulletin with the finish schedule and plan. For every changed room, give me the level, room number, existing floor finish, proposed floor finish, and source page. List conflicting names in the same row. If the bulletin leaves a finish undecided, mark it open.


For 214, the useful result is a single row containing both names, the previous and proposed finishes, and the bulletin page that authorizes the switch. If the schedule has a second row for 214, keep both visible until someone resolves the duplicate. A short, traceable list is easier for the interiors lead to approve than a freshly rewritten schedule.


## What the Gemini 4 Hydrogen benchmarks say about CAD work


Google reports a **53.4% score for Hydrogen on Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA)** , a Google DeepMind benchmark also evaluated by Artificial Analysis. The benchmark asks agents to use visually dense source files to produce work such as spreadsheets, reports, and marked-up drawings. Its headline measure gives weight to the harder requirements in each task. That makes it relevant to following a finish change across documents. It measures a broader set of work than room schedules alone.[Google’s reported Hydrogen score](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-hydrogen/) and[Artificial Analysis’s benchmark methodology](https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/mka)


For a sense of how the model handles geometry, PartForge publishes individual CAD trials. Its compact Hydrogen configuration scored **100 on all three drawer-divider attempts** , while all three attempts to reconstruct a handle from a mesh in Blender failed a required check. The individual cases tell a drafter more than the overall score alone. Matching a room number across files, building a divider, and reconstructing a handle from a mesh each ask the model to do different work.[PartForge’s Hydrogen task results](https://www.partforge.ai/evals/models/gemini-4-hydrogen-google)


## Apply the approved finish change in Revit or AutoCAD


The interiors lead can take that approved row into ArchiLabs Desktop with the marked-up plan. In Revit, ask Desktop to update the floor-finish field that feeds the room schedule. If the project also models finish floors as separate elements, identify the floor in 214 as a second edit. A schedule can say “terrazzo” while the floor geometry still carries the carpet material.


For an AutoCAD finish plan, point Desktop to the finish tag inside Room 214 and give it the new code. The legend entry for the carpet still serves the three offices down the hall. A request tied to the room keeps that shared entry useful. Open the plotted finish plan alongside the schedule, find 214 on each, and the interiors lead can see exactly what the contractor will receive.[Try ArchiLabs Desktop with a marked-up drawing](https://archilabs.ai/desktop)
